claude.sample_unit: clinical infection control scenarios (165 outputs rated by 16 experts)

links.outcome: Clinical knowledge errors and incomplete differentials in LLM infection control recommendations, qualitatively reviewed
links.effect: Critical deficiencies in all models: DeepSeek V3 recommended TB treatment without considering NTM; GPT-4.1 wrongly advised against single-room isolation for MDRA; wrong C. auris screening sites.
links.quote: These findings, summarized in Table 6 , reveal that even the higher-performing models may generate clinically significant and potentially unsafe recommendations.

links.outcome: Effect of structured prompt template vs open-ended prompt on expert-rated output quality
links.effect: Structured prompting gave small significant composite improvement; evidence quality improved (p<0.001), other criteria not significantly changed. Gemini failed structured prompt in 50% of scenarios.
links.quote: The analysis of the structured prompt’s effect revealed that this approach led to a small but statistically significant improvement in the composite score across all LLMs.

links.outcome: Inaccurate LLM infection control recommendations versus expert panel corrections
links.effect: Qualitative review found factual inaccuracies and unsafe advice across all three models despite generally positive scores (composite means 36.77, 36.25, 33.22).
links.quote: These errors highlight potential safety risks and limited real-world applicability, despite generally positive scores.

links.outcome: Reliability of LLM outputs for autonomous use versus adjunct use in infection control
links.effect: Critical errors found in all models; authors conclude LLMs are not reliable for autonomous use and should serve as adjuncts.
links.quote: While GPT-4.1 and DeepSeek V3 deliver useful IPC advice, they are not yet reliable for autonomous use.

unlisted_practices: Structured two-phase prompt template with clarifying questions to improve evidence quality of LLM outputs

links.effect: GPT-4.1 MD=3.58 and DeepSeek V3 MD=3.06 significantly outperformed Gemini; both p < 0.001.
links.quote: For the composite quality score, both GPT-4.1 (mean difference [MD] = 3.58, 95% CI 2.88–4.28, p < 0.001) and DeepSeek V3 (MD = 3.06, 95% CI 2.36–3.75, p < 0.001) significantly outperformed Gemini 2.5 Pro Exp.

links.effect: Composite score improved overall (p = 0.019); evidence quality improved +0.765, +1.106, and +0.425 with p < 0.001.
links.quote: The analysis of the structured prompt’s effect revealed that this approach led to a small but statistically significant improvement in the composite score across all LLMs.

links.outcome: Expert review detection of unsafe outputs
links.effect: Sixteen human evaluators reviewed 165 output sets; qualitative review identified critical deficiencies across all three LLMs.
links.quote: Beyond the quantitative scores, our qualitative review identified critical deficiencies across all three LLMs.

links.effect: Gemini’s Candida auris answer was confusing/impractical; DeepSeek V3 recommended TB treatment from positive AFB smear while overlooking nontuberculous mycobacteria.
links.quote: For example, Gemini 2.5 Pro Exp provided a confusing and impractical response regarding Candida auris de-escalation, while DeepSeek V3 suggested immediate tuberculosis treatment based solely on a positive AFB smear, overlooking alternatives such as nontuberculous mycobacteria.

links.effect: GPT-4.1 advised against single-room isolation for MDRA; Table 6 rated potential harm as High.
links.quote: Even the better performing GPT-4.1 was not immune to error, incorrectly advising against single-room isolation for a patient colonized with MDRA, a recommendation that contradicts standard infection control policy.

unlisted_practices: Assessing how evaluator profession and seniority affect ratings of LLM clinical recommendations.

links.effect: Structured prompting significantly improved composite score (p = 0.019) and evidence quality (p < 0.001) across LLMs compared to open-ended inquiry, with no significant difference for other criteria.
links.quote: The analysis of the structured prompt’s effect revealed that this approach led to a small but statistically significant improvement in the composite score across all LLMs.

links.effect: Qualitative review revealed critical deficiencies across all models, including advising against mandatory single-room isolation for MDRA (GPT-4.1) and initiating empiric TB treatment without considering NTM (DeepSeek V3).
links.quote: Common themes included poor clinical judgment such as recommending aggressive measures for a low-suspicion case and providing factually incorrect advice that contradicted standard infection control policies, particularly regarding multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter species (MDRA) isolation.
